nonCompliants.correctiveActionPlan:
[REDACTED] whom were assigned to 
T1, (both teacher qualified). 
Unknown to [REDACTED] that [REDACTED] was having a difficult day and refused to participate in the daily routines and activities. 
[REDACTED] tried calling the front office to inform the director that [REDACTED] needed support, but the director was in another classroom. Being desperate to get some support in [REDACTED] class of [REDACTED] children left the class to try to find the program director. 
Once the program director was located and realized what had taken place, 
The program director discussed with both [REDACTED] classroom ratio and went over the proper protocols to notify the director of classroom issues. 
[REDACTED] were instructed to contact the director by the intercom system.
During our November 2025 mandatory monthly meeting we went over our classroom ratios, The protocols to handle an uncomfortable work environment and how to properly use the phone/intercom system.
nonCompliants.statementOfNonCompliant: On one occasion in July 2025, an assistant educator was left alone with children in the [REDACTED] classroom. Assistant Teacher. Must be at least 16 years of age or have a high school diploma or equivalent; must work at all times under the direct supervision of at least a teacher qualified staff person.

nonCompliants.correctiveActionPlan:
During my conversation with the investigator
the program director mentioned being in a Conduct meeting with a parent, when [REDACTED] teacher called to get bathroom coverage. The director asked where the children awake, the [REDACTED] teacher stated that all the children were napping, the director then told the [REDACTED] teacher that [REDACTED] could run to the bathroom, but to call [REDACTED] when [REDACTED] returns from the bathroom.
The director made that decision based on a November 6, 2024 policy advisory regarding supervision of [REDACTED] children during nap time. Effective January 1, 2025.
The program director later spoke with the investigator via telephone and [REDACTED] explained that this was a noncompliance. The investigator then went over how to properly use this policy advisory.
The program director now understands that there has to be a reason that the [REDACTED] teachers are covering themselves and that it must be documented prior to; by documenting the need on the daily schedule.
nonCompliants.statementOfNonCompliant: Through statements, it has been identified that educators have left their classrooms on occasion without coverage to use the bathroom, leaving their co-educator alone and out of ratio. Fixed Age Groups. Children may be assigned to groups with others within their same age range, as specified by the Department provided the requirements of 606 CMR 7.10(9)(b)1-6 are met. nonCompliants.correctiveActionPlan:
1) [REDACTED] had a one on one plan for improvement meeting. During this meeting [REDACTED] was able to reflect and process through what they felt would help ensure positive guidance would be used at all times as well as understanding that asking for support during stressful times should be seen a strength not a weakness.   

2) During transition times the classroom will be provided with additional staff to support the classroom.

3) Additionally during the next two monthly staff meetings all staff will participate in a mandatory Professional Development that will focus on use of Positive Guidance Techniques and how to use them in situations that our staff have identified as stressful situations in the individual classrooms.
nonCompliants.statementOfNonCompliant: The investigation found reasonable cause to believe that [REDACTED] did not use positive guidance techniques when redirecting a child's behavior. While working in [REDACTED] classroom, [REDACTED] observed [REDACTED] trying to bite another child. [REDACTED] brought [REDACTED] to the rug by one arm in a forceful manner. [REDACTED] stated that they did not realize they had forcefully moved [REDACTED] to the rug area until they reviewed the classroom surveillance video. Educators must provide guidance to children in a positive and consistent way based on an understanding of the individual needs and development of children by encouraging self-control and using positive child guidance techniques such as recognizing and reinforcing children's appropriate behaviors, having reasonable and positive expectations and using environmental modifications, activity modifications, adult or peer support, and other teaching strategies to encourage appropriate behavior and prevent challenging behaviors.

nonCompliants.correctiveActionPlan:
in January 2023 we did our annual registration at this time. They mentioned child parent lost their job and took a leave of absence from Agape when they returned we asked for an updated enrollment packet food program as well as an updated physical. We received the physical but did not receive the updated registration packet
To correct this situation, we have amended our parent handbook for leaves of absences. Parents must Give a notice as early as possible. Upon Each child’s return A new enrollment packet, new food program And an updated physical must Be completed before the children return.
nonCompliants.statementOfNonCompliant: One child's file did not have the proper updated information. Upon review, the file was missing updated releases and physical information. The program was able to locate the physical, but there were several months when releases had expired. Programs were required to keep ongoing records up to date.

nonCompliants.correctiveActionPlan:
on November 6, 2024 a team member observed a child falling on the ground during a time in [REDACTED]where all the children were seated at the table getting ready for their lunches. The team member immediately came to the program director to inform [REDACTED] had witnessed something, but wasn’t sure of what [REDACTED] saw and could [REDACTED] review it in the cameras. when the program director reviewed the said incident, [REDACTED] observed to other children being mistreated. The director immediately went to the classroom to see the children and make sure that they were physically OK. [REDACTED] then asked [REDACTED] to observe what [REDACTED] had just seen on the cameras. [REDACTED] immediately apologize and asked for the directors forgiveness and swore that [REDACTED]would never do that again. The director briefly went over the child guidance policy and asked [REDACTED] to get her belongings and that [READCTED] needed to leave the premises. the program director then contacted [REDACTED] program licenser [REDACTED] The director then entered the reports into the portal.
The program director personally contact each parent, informing them of the incident and asked if [REDACTED] could have a brief meeting with them at pick up. [REDACTED] assured them that their children were physically OK but wanted to meet with them to discuss their concerns. A suspension letter was then sent by email to [REDACTED]. The {[REDACTED] polic took a report from the assistant director. At the end of the day the program director met with each parent as they came in to pick up their child. They talked about the incident how it was handled would the educator be returning and most of all they wanted to make sure that [REDACTED] didn’t work in childcare again.
nonCompliants.statementOfNonCompliant: On 11/6/2024, [REDACTED] was not nurturing towards three of the children.  They did not demonstrate proper child guidance or effective communication when interacting with three children.  [REDACTED] conducted themselves in a way that resulted in a 51A being on them for abuse.

nonCompliants.correctiveActionPlan:
Agape Child Care has always held the highest child guidance standard.
On 11/6/2024 a team member thought they saw something, and [REDACTED] immediately said something to the program director. From there we acted swiftly to protect the safety of the classroom students from experiencing further abusive treatment from [REDACTED]
This was an unfortunate situation and We will not tolerate this kind of behavior towards children.
nonCompliants.statementOfNonCompliant: [REDACTED] was prohibited from inflicting any abuse upon a child.  They were required to operate in a way that protected children from abuse however their actions demonstrated abuse toward three children.

nonCompliants.correctiveActionPlan: On the second day of employment [REDACTED] witnessed abusive interactions between [REDACTED] and three students. The program, director asked [REDACTED] what [REDACTED] had witnessed, and [REDACTED] reply was that [REDACTED]saw nothing, but after the program director observed the camera footage, [REDACTED] asked [REDACTED] why [REDACTED] said that [REDACTED] did not see what happened on all three counts. [REDACTED] explain that [REDACTED] was afraid to say anything because [REDACTED] thought [REDACTED] would get fired at that time the program director went over the child guidance and the abuse and neglect policies. to make sure that[REDACTED] understood EEC regulations, Agape policies and expectations.
nonCompliants.statementOfNonCompliant: [REDACTED] was in the classroom and witnessed [REDACTED] inappropriate responses towards three children.  [REDACTED] did not report the abusive actions that were documented on camera.

nonCompliants.correctiveActionPlan:
Agape was happy to hear that all three counts of abuse and neglect was supported. We have worked hard to educate our teachers on recognizing inappropriate behavior amongst educators. We speak often on letting the team know if you see something, say something, we have also worked on how to stop burnout for teachers in the classroom. When you feel frustrated or aggravated to call for help. 
We are so sorry that this unbelievable treatment of children happened to our three students. We will work hard to bring more trainings to support our child guidance policy and give our teacher's the proper tools to handle challenging behaviors in the classrooms.
nonCompliants.statementOfNonCompliant: The allegations of physical abuse by [REDACTED] were supported on behalf of all three children.

The staff member became preoccupied with the safety of the children in her classroom at that time and wanted to tell me when things were not so chaotic.

visitDomainList.description: A Background Check (BRC) shall be performed on all candidates.
visitDomainList.regulationArticle: EEC’s BRC regulations are designed to ensure the completion of BRCs on individuals subject to EEC’s oversight, including those in receipt of federal Child Care Development Fund (CCDF) funding pursuant to the Child Care Development Block Grant (CCDBG) Act of 2014 at 42 USC § 9858 and funding through the Families First Prevention Services Act of 2017 at 42 USC § 471(a)(20)(D). Further, BRCs shall be performed in accordance with the statutory framework of M.G.L. c. 15D, §§ 7 and 8, 606 CMR 14.00 and consistent with the timelines established by EEC regulations or policy. EEC is responsible for reviewing all disqualifying information for candidates, with the exception of candidates for adoptive and foster parents to the extent authorized by the Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI) and state statute. EEC may delegate to another Commonwealth entity its authority to complete BRCs through a Memorandum of Understanding or other applicable agreement to the extent permitted by state and federal law. While effective immediately, EEC will implement the provisions of 606 CMR 14.00 in phases and provide updated timetables for implementation within its written policies. Nothing in 606 CMR 14.00 shall be construed to create a private right of action if an EEC licensed, approved or funded program has acted in accordance with 606 CMR 14.00 and any policies adopted thereunder.

visitDomainList.correctionPlan:
Corrective Action Plan – EpiPen Medication Intake

As part of our corrective action plan for receiving EpiPen medications from parents, staff will verify the contents of each EpiPen package at the time of receipt. Staff will confirm that each package contains two (2) EpiPen auto-injectors and, if included, one trainer (tester) device.

To prevent future errors, staff will visually inspect and distinguish the trainer device from the actual EpiPen auto-injectors before accepting the medication. This additional verification step has been implemented because, in this instance, the trainer (tester) was mistakenly identified as an actual EpiPen.

visitDomainList.description: A Background Check (BRC) shall be performed on all candidates.
visitDomainList.indicator: BRCs on all potential employees - R Sep 2025
visitDomainList.regulationArticle: EEC’s BRC regulations are designed to ensure the completion of BRCs on individuals subject to EEC’s oversight, including those in receipt of federal Child Care Development Fund (CCDF) funding pursuant to the Child Care Development Block Grant (CCDBG) Act of 2014 at 42 USC § 9858 and funding through the Families First Prevention Services Act of 2017 at 42 USC § 471(a)(20)(D). Further, BRCs shall be performed in accordance with the statutory framework of M.G.L. c. 15D, §§ 7 and 8, 606 CMR 14.00 and consistent with the timelines established by EEC regulations or policy. EEC is responsible for reviewing all disqualifying information for candidates, with the exception of candidates for adoptive and foster parents to the extent authorized by the Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI) and state statute. EEC may delegate to another Commonwealth entity its authority to complete BRCs through a Memorandum of Understanding or other applicable agreement to the extent permitted by state and federal law. While effective immediately, EEC will implement the provisions of 606 CMR 14.00 in phases and provide updated timetables for implementation within its written policies. Nothing in 606 CMR 14.00 shall be construed to create a private right of action if an EEC licensed, approved or funded program has acted in accordance with 606 CMR 14.00 and any policies adopted thereunder.

visitDomainList.indicator: Individual Health Care Plan (IHCP) - R Apr 2025
visitDomainList.regulationArticle: Individual Health Care Plans  The licensee must maintain as part of a childs record, an individual health care plan for each child with a chronic medical condition, which has been diagnosed by a licensed health care practitioner.  The plan must describe the chronic condition, its symptoms, any medical treatment that may be necessary while the child is in care, the potential side effects of that treatment, and the potential consequences to the childs health if the treatment is not administered.

visitDomainList.description: Emergency evacuation observations
visitDomainList.regulationArticle: The educator must hold practice evacuation drills with all groups of children and all educators from each floor level of the approved space at least monthly.  Drills must be held during different times of the program day, and must use alternative exits.  The educator must document the date, time, exit route used, number of children evacuated and effectiveness of each drill.
